title: Daily SGS Top 5
tagline: Five stories, one question: who's in control?

stories.headline: World Bank says corruption is holding Kenya back
stories.summary: Corruption costs Kenya about 2% of GDP a year. 39% of firms call it a major problem, up from 25% in 2013.
stories.label: Slightly Globalist
stories.why: A global lender sets the reform agenda before Kenya's 2027 election.
stories.what_it_means: Strong reforms could make the economy 22.3% bigger by 2035 and add up to 7.7 million better jobs.
stories.economic_impact: More borrowing at higher cost; 2026 growth forecast raised to 4.6%.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a leaky bucket that never fills up.

stories.headline: Oracle drops a $7 billion AI chip deal with China's Tencent
stories.summary: Oracle cancelled a five-year lease giving Tencent about 100,000 AI chips in Southeast Asia after US officials raised concerns. Reported by the FT; not yet confirmed.
stories.label: Moderately Sovereign
stories.why: Governments, not markets, decide who gets critical tech.
stories.what_it_means: Washington and Beijing are both pulling key tech back inside their own borders.
stories.economic_impact: Oracle loses a big contract; Chinese firms lose a back door to top chips.
stories.everyday_example: It's like two neighbors telling their kids to stop sharing toys over the fence.

stories.headline: Iran picks which countries' ships can pass Hormuz
stories.summary: An Iranian lawmaker says ships from India, China, Iraq and Qatar are exempt from Hormuz limits. India and China still pay fees.
stories.label: Moderately Globalist
stories.why: One country takes control of a shared energy route and picks favorites.
stories.what_it_means: Iran is treating a world shipping lane as its own gate.
stories.economic_impact: Relief for India's oil imports, but Brent is still about $104 a barrel.
stories.everyday_example: It's like a bouncer letting his friends skip the line, and still charging most of them.

stories.headline: Britain and the EU finalize a deal to cut Brexit food checks
stories.summary: The UK and EU finished a food-trade deal ahead of a Nov 20 summit. Britain follows EU food rules again.
stories.label: Moderately Globalist
stories.why: A nation accepts a bloc's rules it doesn't get to write.
stories.what_it_means: A big step back toward Brussels to drop border paperwork.
stories.economic_impact: Exporters skip £200 vet certificates; fresh sausages and shellfish can be sold to the EU again.
stories.everyday_example: It's like moving out, then following your parents' rules to keep using the fridge.

stories.headline: Democrats win the House and Senate
stories.summary: AP says Democrats took both chambers, flipping at least seven Senate seats. Trump says he accepts the results.
stories.label: Neutral
stories.what_it_means: Split government for Trump's last two years.
stories.economic_impact: Stock futures rose; a split Congress usually means fewer big new laws.
stories.everyday_example: It's like the staff voting in a new manager for half the office.
